title: Repairing a Rocking Toilet: Flange Security, Wax Seal, and Shim Techniques
summary: The video explains why a toilet rocks and how to fix it by first securing the toilet flange to a solid floor with non-ferrous fasteners, ensuring the wax seal remains properly seated, and addressing uneven floors or water leaks with shimming. It emphasizes that the toilet must sit flat and be properly anchored to prevent stress on the seal and piping, and it presents practical shim options—plastic shims or non-rusting spacers (even coins) when traditional shims aren’t available—while advising to trim shims so they stay hidden and to avoid rust-prone or wooden shims in wet areas. The overall goal is to stabilize the toilet to prevent leaks, sewer gas entry, and pipe movement.
topics: Shim placement under the dip area

sections.title: Flange security and the wax seal
sections.description: Explain how tightening closet bolts without securing the flange to a solid floor will still allow rocking; emphasize securing the flange to the structure with non-ferrous screws so the flange doesn’t pull up and the toilet stays stable. Highlight the wax seal as essential to prevent water and sewer gas leaks once the toilet is stable.

sections.title: Root causes of rocking: floor and leaks
sections.description: Describe common real-world issues that cause rocking—water leaks or an uneven/crooked floor due to settlement—and how these affect stability and sealing surfaces.

sections.title: Shim the toilet to restore level
sections.description: Advise placing plastic shims under the toilet where the floor dips to prevent rocking and reduce stress on connections; shims can be trimmed so they are hidden and flush with the surface.

sections.title: Alternative spacers and final cautions
concepts: no wood shims in wet areas
sections.description: If plastic shims aren’t available, use something that won’t rust (e.g., coins) to fill gaps and stabilize the toilet. Avoid wood shims in wet areas and emphasize understanding the underlying mechanics to maintain a stable, leak-free install.

featured_techniques.technique: Securing the toilet flange to the subfloor with non-ferrous screws to prevent rocking
Evaluating and maintaining the wax seal (wax ring) to prevent leaks
Shim the toilet to compensate for floor irregularities
Use plastic shims and trim them flush under the toilet
Use non-rusting spacers or coins as a substitute for shims when needed
Avoid rust-prone or wooden shims in wet areas
